newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-PAPIN AUCTION TO HELP HANDICAPPED CHILDREN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PAPIN AUCTION TO HELP HANDICAPPED CHILDREN.

text.p: Jean-Pierre Papin, whose little daughter Emilie suffered brain damage at birth, has helped organise an auction next week of sports memorabilia in aid of handicapped children.

"(The parents) are often on their own, discouraged and haven't the same financial means as us. So, if we can, (we will) help them," the Bordeaux centre forward, whose wife also had a part in creating the Nine of Hearts Foundation, said.
Emilie is undergoing an American method of treatment that involves great expense and frequent trips to the United States.
"It's a restricting method and not a miracle solution ... With Emilie, it's working. She has made enormous progress and I live only for that," the former France captain said.

Papin has rounded up sports equipment belonging to leading figures in world sports, travelling to Imola for contributions from racing drivers Jean Alesi and Jacques Villeneuve and also obtaining the late Ayrton Senna's last helmet.

Jerseys belonging to soccer greats Michel Platini, Roberto Baggio and Eric Cantona and basketball's Magic Johnson, a pair of gloves worn by the late world boxing champion Carlos Monzon and tennis gear from Thomas Muster, Stefan Edberg and Mary Pierce will also go under the hammer in a televised auction in Bordeaux on Monday.
